packet.headline_seed: Fireworks, flyovers and a 'really long' Trump speech ahead as US celebrates 250th
packet.description_seed: The celebrations in the US capital will feature 850,000 fireworks, a "really long" speech from the president and scorching temperatures.

clean_source_blocks.text: The celebrations in the US capital will feature 850,000 fireworks, a "really long" speech from the president and scorching temperatures.

Speaking at the Mount Rushmore national monument in South Dakota on Friday, the president warned of a resurgence of what he called "the communist menace" and "newcomers" who embraced ideas opposed to the American way of life. His comments reflect a growing political line of attack ahead of the November mid-term elections, with Republicans seeking to brand Democrats as communists. The Washington DC event, formally known as the Salute to America 250 Celebrations & Fireworks - is due to begin at 19:00 local time, with Trump expected to speak a few hours later at approximately 21:45. He has promised to make a "really long speech" at the Fourth of July festivities, despite the heatwave, "to show that I can do anything". Trump's new take on 250 years of American expansionism After 250 years the American Dream i ---

'Could be worse' - Americans on the state of the nation in its 250th year US President Donald Trump will head to Washington DC's National Mall on Saturday for what he has billed as a "spectacular rally" celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The event, taking place as a sweltering heatwave grips swathes of the eastern and central US, will include flyovers by hundreds of aircraft and a fireworks display organisers hope will be the biggest of all time. Military flyovers over Washington DC will happen every hour between 13:15 local time (17:15 GMT) and sunset, the organisers said, and Trump's new Air Force One will feature in one of the formations over the capital. The president, however, has been accused by opponents of politicising the nation's anniversary event and several music acts dropped out soon after being announced.

Trump touted America as a unique and strong nation whose best days are ahead of it in a speech at Mount Rushmore ahead of tomorrow’s celebration in Washington, D.C. Washington, D.C.’s “Salute to America” celebration is expected to draw thousands of people to the National Mall tomorrow for a night full of music, military flyovers, pre-produced videos, a speech by the president and the largest single fireworks display ever produced. But it’s also got something else: the designation as a “National Special Security Event.” Super Bowls, presidential inaugurations, nominating conventions and gatherings of the United Nations General Assembly are typically considered NSSEs — but never before has Washington’s Fourth of July bash qualified as such.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
'Could be worse' - Americans on the state of the nation in its 250th year

US President Donald Trump will head to Washington DC's National Mall on Saturday for what he has billed as a "spectacular rally" celebrating America's 250th anniversary.

The event, taking place as a sweltering heatwave grips swathes of the eastern and central US, will include flyovers by hundreds of aircraft and a fireworks display organisers hope will be the biggest of all time.

Military flyovers over Washington DC will happen every hour between 13:15 local time (17:15 GMT) and sunset, the organisers said, and Trump's new Air Force One will feature in one of the formations over the capital.

The president, however, has been accused by opponents of politicising the nation's anniversary event and several music acts dropped out soon after being announced.

Extremely hot, humid temperatures of approximately 38C (100F) and a later-than-anticipated start time may also have an impact on the size of the crowd that attends.

The intense heat has already led to events being cancelled. On Friday, organisers of the National Park Service's Independence Day Parade in Washington DC said they had cancelled the annual event over ​safety concerns. Some celebration events have also been cancelled from New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Maryland to as far west as Colorado.

There is also the potential for evening thunderstorms that could disrupt the events, which have been organised by a White House-backed public-private partnership.

President Trump used a speech on the eve of Independence Day to claim that American identity is under threat from what he called domestic "radicals" and "extremists".

Speaking at the Mount Rushmore national monument in South Dakota on Friday, the president warned of a resurgence of what he called "the communist menace" and "newcomers" who embraced ideas opposed to the American way of life.

His comments reflect a growing political line of attack ahead of the November mid-term elections, with Republicans seeking to brand Democrats as communists.

The Washington DC event, formally known as the Salute to America 250 Celebrations & Fireworks - is due to begin at 19:00 local time, with Trump expected to speak a few hours later at approximately 21:45.

He has promised to make a "really long speech" at the Fourth of July festivities, despite the heatwave, "to show that I can do anything".

Trump's new take on 250 years of American expansionism

After 250 years the American Dream i

---

[Lähde: NBC News]
Trump touted America as a unique and strong nation whose best days are ahead of it in a speech at Mount Rushmore ahead of tomorrow’s celebration in Washington, D.C.

Washington, D.C.’s “Salute to America” celebration is expected to draw thousands of people to the National Mall tomorrow for a night full of music, military flyovers, pre-produced videos, a speech by the president and the largest single fireworks display ever produced.

But it’s also got something else: the designation as a “National Special Security Event.”

Super Bowls, presidential inaugurations, nominating conventions and gatherings of the United Nations General Assembly are typically considered NSSEs — but never before has Washington’s Fourth of July bash qualified as such.

The designation allows the Department of Homeland Security to designate the Secret Service as the lead agency securing the event and helps ensure coordination among the FBI, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and what we expect to be dozens of state, local and federal agencies.

In addition to those agencies — everyone from D.C. police to the Coast Guard to D.C. Fire to the U.S. Park Police — there are more than 4,800 members of the National Guard from 23 states and the District of Columbia on the streets of Washington.

Miles of fencing surround the Mall, and dozens of street closures and roadblocks will make travel downtown nearly impossible.

There will be TSA-style security greeting the public at both the Great American State Fair and the Salute to America sites, both delayed in their opening tomorrow because of the oppressive heat.

But that TSA-style security will greatly affect the experience of people on the Mall during what is typically a day of family fun.

It means, among other things: no balls, Frisbees, coolers, folding chairs, metal drink tumblers or aerosols (including sunscreen).

During a security briefing Monday, the assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Washington field office, Darren Cox, told reporters authorities are “not tracking any credible threats.”

U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said the same at an unrelated media event yesterday. “I’m not tracking anything in terms of the threat environment. We’re all hoping that Americans are able to celebrate, whether they’re in D.C. or around the country,” she said.

payload.title: Yhdysvaltain 250-vuotisjuhla tuo Washingtoniin ylilentoja, ilotulituksen ja Trumpin pitkän puheen
payload.summary: Washingtonissa järjestettävä Yhdysvaltain 250-vuotisjuhla kokoaa lauantaina väkeä National Mallille. Ohjelmassa on sotilasilmailua, musiikkia, videoesityksiä, presidentti Donald Trumpin puhe ja järjestäjien mukaan ennätyksellisen suuri ilotulitus.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain pääkaupungissa Washingtonissa järjestetään lauantaina suuri 250-vuotisjuhla, jonka ohjelmaan kuuluvat sotilasilmailun ylilennot, musiikki, videoesitykset, presidentti Donald Trumpin puhe ja järjestäjien mukaan kaikkien aikojen suurimmaksi suunniteltu ilotulitus. Tapahtuma osuu itäistä ja keskistä Yhdysvaltoja koettelevan helleaallon keskelle, ja sen odotetaan keräävän tuhansia ihmisiä National Mallille.

## Juhlasta odotetaan näyttävää

Washingtonin tapahtuma tunnetaan nimellä Salute to America 250 Celebrations & Fireworks. Sen on määrä alkaa kello 19 paikallista aikaa, ja Trumpin odotetaan puhuvan muutamaa tuntia myöhemmin noin kello 21.45. Presidentti on luvannut pitää neljännen heinäkuuta juhlassa ”todella pitkän puheen” helteestä huolimatta ja kuvannut tilaisuutta näyttäväksi kokoontumiseksi.

Järjestäjien mukaan Washingtonin yllä nähdään päivän aikana satoja ilma-aluksia. Sotilaallisia ylilentoja on tarkoitus järjestää tunnin välein kello 13.15 paikallista aikaa alkaen auringonlaskuun saakka. Yhdessä muodostelmassa nähdään myös presidentin uusi Air Force One.

Ilotulituksesta odotetaan poikkeuksellisen laajaa. Juhlallisuuksiin on kerrottu kuuluvan 850 000 ilotulitetta, ja järjestäjät tavoittelevat maailman suurinta yksittäistä ilotulitusnäytöstä. Ohjelmaan kuuluu myös ennalta tuotettuja videoita sekä musiikkiesityksiä.

## Politiikka seuraa juhlapäivää

Trump puhui ennen Washingtonin juhlaa Mount Rushmoren kansallisella muistomerkillä Etelä-Dakotassa. Hän kuvasi Yhdysvaltoja ainutlaatuiseksi ja vahvaksi maaksi, jonka parhaat päivät ovat hänen mukaansa edessä. Samassa yhteydessä hän varoitti ”kommunistisesta uhasta” ja arvosteli tulokkaita, joiden hän sanoi omaksuneen amerikkalaiselle elämäntavalle vastakkaisia ajatuksia.

Kommentit sopivat republikaanien voimistuvaan poliittiseen hyökkäyslinjaan ennen marraskuun välivaaleja, joissa puolue pyrkii leimaamaan demokraatteja kommunisteiksi. Presidenttiä on myös syytetty kansallisen vuosipäivän politisoimisesta, ja useita musiikkiesiintyjiä vetäytyi tapahtumasta pian sen jälkeen, kun heidän osallistumisensa oli julkistettu.

## Turvallisuusluokitus on poikkeuksellinen

Washingtonin juhla on saanut National Special Security Event -luokituksen. Vastaava nimitys annetaan tavallisesti esimerkiksi Super Bowlille, presidentin virkaanastujaisille, puoluekokouksille ja YK:n yleiskokouksen kokoontumisille. Lähdeaineiston mukaan Washingtonin neljännen heinäkuuta juhlalle tällaista luokitusta ei ole aiemmin annettu.
summary_bullets: Ohjelmassa on sotilasilmailun ylilentoja, musiikkia, videoita, Trumpin puhe ja suuri ilotulitus.
Tapahtuma on saanut poikkeuksellisen turvallisuusluokituksen ja herättänyt kritiikkiä politisoitumisesta.

Lähdeaineiston mukaan Washingtonin neljännen heinäkuuta juhlalle tällaista luokitusta ei ole aiemmin annettu.

The celebrations in the US capital will feature 850,000 fireworks, a "really long" speech from the president and scorching temperatures.

Speaking at the Mount Rushmore national monument in South Dakota on Friday, the president warned of a resurgence of what he called "the communist menace" and "newcomers" who embraced ideas opposed to the American way of life. His comments reflect a growing political line of attack ahead of the November mid-term elections, with Republicans seeking to brand Democrats as communists. The Washington DC event, formally known as the Salute to America 250 Celebrations & Fireworks - is due to begin at 19:00 local time, with Trump expected to speak a few hours later at approximately 21:45. He has promised to make a "really long speech" at the Fourth of July festivities, despite the heatwave, "to show that I can do anything". 'Could be worse' - Americans on the state of the nation in its 250th year US President Donald Trump will head to Washington DC's National Mall on Saturday for what he has billed as a "spectacular rally" celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The event, taking place as a sweltering heatwave grips swathes of the eastern and central US, will include flyovers by hundreds of aircraft and a fireworks display organisers hope will be the biggest of all time. Military flyovers over Washington DC will happen every hour between 13:15 local time (17:15 GMT) and sunset, the organisers said, and Trump's new Air Force One will feature in one of the formations over the capital. The president, however, has been accused by opponents of politicising the nation's anniversary event and several music acts dropped out soon after being announced.

Trump touted America as a unique and strong nation whose best days are ahead of it in a speech at Mount Rushmore ahead of tomorrow’s celebration in Washington, D.C. Washington, D.C.’s “Salute to America” celebration is expected to draw thousands of people to the National Mall tomorrow for a night full of music, military flyovers, pre-produced videos, a speech by the president and the largest single fireworks display ever produced. But it’s also got something else: the designation as a “National Special Security Event.” Super Bowls, presidential inaugurations, nominating conventions and gatherings of the United Nations General Assembly are typically considered NSSEs — but never before has Washington’s Fourth of July bash qualified as such.
